descriptions..claude/agents/templates/skills/read-sec: New (ST-000044): a Claude Code skill (`.claude/skills/read-section/SKILL.md` once deployed — sibling of `.claude/agents/`, not nested under it) that gives a self-contained, corrected recipe for extracting one numbered section from a Markdown file cited as `<File>.md §N`. Fixes issue #127: a bare `§N` citation with no attached command had no way to compute a partial-read range, so agents fell back to reading the whole file; and the inline-sed convention some deployments hand-rolled (`sed -n '/^## N\./,/^## N+1\./p'`) is inclusive at both ends, so it always leaks the next heading line. Skills are auto-surfaced to every Claude Code session via the harness's own skill listing, so this is discoverable without reading any rules file first — the exact chicken-and-egg gap the issue names. Generalized in the same version (issue #118 follow-up, no separate version bump): broadened the frontmatter description and recipe to cover any consistent heading prefix, not just numbered `§N` citations, and added a worked example for `### Fact N` archive headings, so the two-tier memory pilot's archive retrieval (`Agent_Common.md §12`) can point at this one skill instead of re-deriving the recipe inline. Working mirror (`.claude/skills/read-section/SKILL.md`) carries the identical change. Fixed later in the same version (issue #142, no separate version bump): the section-extraction recipe mapped a `§Na` citation to a `### Na` heading and told the agent to grep `^### [0-9]+[a-z]\.` — a marker narrowed to the target's own shape. In a file holding exactly one sub-numbered heading that grep returns a single hit, so step 2 takes its "last heading" branch and the extraction runs to end of file, silently swallowing every following section (measured: a 53% over-read, no error). Replaced with one flat marker for the whole family, `^## ([0-9]+[a-z]?\.|Version)`, matching §N, §Na and the `## Version` footer alike, plus an explicit rule never to narrow the marker to the target's own shape. The worked example was rebuilt: the prior one cited `Agent_Common.md §5` (a file #134 later deleted), and the example now demonstrates both failure directions (over-read from a narrowed marker, short read from a bare `^## ` that hits unnumbered sub-headings inside a numbered section). Working mirror carries the identical recipe. Fixed later in the same version (ST-000132, no separate version bump): the worked example was rebuilt again to cite `Agent_Common_Read_On_Demand_template.md §1` — `Agent_Common_template.md` is the file #134 deleted, split into the two files below.

Holds Pre-Work Sequence (with Working Record folded in, same treatment as the working mirror), Secret Handling, Token-Efficiency Conventions, External Content Handling, and a new On-Demand Records Routing Table (§5). Read in full every spawn, never section-read. Same split mirrored under `.antigravity/agents/templates/rules/` (outside this manifest's `.claude`-only scope).

New (ST-000132, no separate version bump): on-demand tier of the former `Agent_Common_template.md` — Project Memory (§1), Troubleshooting Protocol (§2), End-of-Work Retrospective (§3), Stage-Transition Commit (§5), Credential-Gated Verification (§6). §4 is a deliberate numbering gap (where the pre-split Working Record section sat before it folded into `Agent_Common_Bootstrap_template.md §1`), matching the working mirror's identical gap so a stale citation resolves to nothing rather than a different rule. Fetched section-by-section via the `read-section` skill, never read in full. Same split mirrored under `.antigravity/agents/templates/rules/`.

No subagent needs to read it — every spawn is auto-injected the full CLAUDE.md by the harness, so trimming CLAUDE.md down to what every role needs removes a fixed per-spawn context cost (measured ~20% actual-token reduction on a repeat cold-start Dev implementation, N=1 each side). descriptions..claude/agents/templates/rules/Story_Sta: Fix (ST-000038): issue comments were the only capped artifact with no enforcement. §12 gains a third gate, **Commenter — Before Posting an Issue Comment**, turning the ~150–200 word cap into a `wc -w` self-check (the same move `wc -c` made for memory files). §9 writing rules: one-topic-per-comment promoted out of the threading block into numbered rule 2 as a constraint on composition (with an explicit carve-out that batching replies to questions asked together is permitted); rule 4 now prohibits pasting command output, check transcripts, or verification logs, scoped to issue and PR comments alike, with a single named carve-out — gate-mandated CI evidence, i.e. the literal `gh pr checks` output the §12 Reviewer gate requires in a PR approval comment — so the two rules can both be obeyed; the §12 Reviewer and Commenter gates cross-reference the carve-out from both sides; new rule 5 'body edits are announced, not reproduced' — a comment states which section changed and why, never the resulting body text, because a duplicated wording goes stale on the next edit and then contradicts the body. Round 3 adds the drafting target the gate was missing: §9 rule 3 now says draft to the shape (one short paragraph per topic — decision, one-line why, pointer) so the `wc -w` check is a backstop that should almost never fire, and the §12 Commenter gate splits into a before-you-draft item and before-you-post items, with an explicit instruction not to trim-and-recount when the count fails (an over-length draft is usually a bundled topic or a pasted transcript — remove something whole instead). Measured cause: a single 200-word comment cost 22% of one agent run because the post-hoc check induced a draft-then-truncate loop, each pass re-reading full context.
descriptions..claude/agents/templates/rules/Agent_Com: Fix (ST-000038): §2 rule 4 'Point, don't mirror' scoped to issue comments as well as memory writes — re-deriving a recorded fact is more expensive in a comment, which every downstream role re-reads. Enforced via the new Commenter gate.
descriptions..claude/agents/templates/rules/Story_Sta: Fix (ST-000038): §9 view carries the same delta as the cross-role source — one-topic-per-comment as a composition rule, `wc -w` cap, transcript prohibition with the gate-mandated-CI-evidence carve-out named for Dev's peer-reviewer role, announce-don't-reproduce, cite-don't-re-explain, plus a pointer to the §12 Commenter gate. Round 3: carries the draft-to-shape target.

Fix (ST-000038): §9 view carries the same delta, with the closer-role failure mode called out explicitly — PO is the only role that edits the story body, so 'announce the edit, never reproduce the new AC text' is stated as its own rule with a worked example. Round 3: carries the draft-to-shape target.

Fix (ST-000038): §9 view carries the same delta. QA's per-AC evidence exemption is preserved and clarified — it exempts the word cap only, not the one-topic or transcript rules, and the gate's `wc -w` item is satisfied by stating the exemption rather than skipping the check. Round 3: carries a role-specific draft-to-shape target — one line per AC (criterion, verdict, pointer), so length follows AC count and never needs trimming.

Fix (ST-000038): §9 view carries the same delta, phrased for the reviewer role that produced the observed 4x-over comment — a finding surfacing mid-review posts as its own comment, and no verification transcript goes inline except the gate-mandated `gh pr checks` output the Reviewer gate requires in a PR approval comment. Round 3: carries the draft-to-shape target.
descriptions..claude/agents/templates/rules/Strict_Mo: Fix (ST-000038): strict mode's local comment-entry writing standard restates §9 verbatim and would otherwise have drifted — same delta applied, with the Commenter gate declared applicable ('issue comment' read as 'comment entry') and the transcript carve-out noted as inapplicable, since strict mode has no PRs. Round 3: carries the draft-to-shape target.

descriptions..claude/agents/templates/shared/workflow: [ST-000028] New `refine prototype` workflow: orchestrator acts as UI/UX Designer directly (no agent spawn) for a lightweight, no-story iteration loop against a `-ui-prototype` companion repo — reuses/creates the repo via Build Software's Path B repo conventions (never its scaffold-generation agent), tracks progress in the target project's `.claude/agents/tmp/refine_prototype_state.md` (not the prototype repo), commits each iteration directly with a `prototype adaptation:` prefix (github mode pushes live, strict mode stays local), and at loop end reuses `Create_Stories_Workflow.md`'s draft-and-confirm step to create stories in the paired production repo's tracker.

descriptions..claude/agents/templates/rules/Story_Sta: [ST-000027] §13 Story Creation Template — bug/defect stories (`bug` label) now add a `## Reproduction` section (`**Repro Command:**`/`**Expected:**`/`**Actual:**`) right after Acceptance Criteria. The new Bug Reproduction Pre-Flight step runs `Repro Command` verbatim before any implementer spawns — never a command parsed from AC prose; absent/`unknown` falls back to the pre-existing behavior (Stage 1 implementer reproduces as part of its own work). Strict mode has no label mechanism, so the section's presence in the story MD is itself the bug-story marker.
descriptions..claude/agents/templates/shared/workflow: [ST-000027] New 'Bug Reproduction Pre-Flight' section runs immediately ahead of Stage 0, for bug-labeled (GitHub) / `## Reproduction`-bearing (strict) stories only. Reproduced → proceeds to Stage 1 with the confirmed repro artifact handed to the implementer. Not reproduced → no agent spawned, repro steps + result reported on the story, status label left unchanged. Two independent skip paths (no usable `Repro Command`, tooling/command unavailable) both fall back to pre-existing behavior unchanged.

[ST-000027] Pipeline state file gains a `Repro Skipped:` field (comma-separated story IDs not reproduced this run) carried forward across per-story state overwrites within a run, cleared on a fresh run; new Pipeline Rule skips re-selecting stories already recorded there — this is how Sprint Workflow implements 'skip and continue' for the not-reproduced outcome from Bug Reproduction Pre-Flight.

[ST-000027] Stage Entry Check's `status:ready`/`status:in-progress` row now runs Bug Reproduction Pre-Flight ahead of Stage 0; a not-reproduced outcome reports to the user and stops the pipeline for the targeted story instead of skip-and-continue (no 'next story' concept in Start Story Workflow).

descriptions..claude/agents/templates/rules/Product_O: [ST-000026] New §11a Roadmap Story Drain: authoring or updating a roadmap/planning doc (Implementation Roadmap, or any `*Roadmap*.md` under `docs/feature/<feature_name>/plan/`) now mandatorily drains every story it defines into a tracked `status:backlog` issue/story at that same moment, instead of deferring to sprint planning. Idempotent via a `**Roadmap Source:** <roadmap-file> :: Phase N :: <story title>` marker line, matched as an exact full body line against candidates (github: `gh issue list --search "... in:body" --state all --json number,body`, treated as a candidate set not a verdict — a bare phrase/search hit can false-positive on a prefix-titled story; strict: grep the stories folder with a whole-line match) before every create — re-authoring the same roadmap returns an existing exact-line match for every story and creates zero duplicates. Cross-references the new `Plan_Sprint_Workflow.md` Stage 1 reconciliation backstop.
descriptions..claude/agents/templates/shared/workflow: [ST-000026] Stage 1 gains a new step 7, 'Roadmap reconciliation backstop' (feature sprints only): before Stage 2 selects candidate stories, checks every roadmap-defined story against tracked issues/stories **in any status** (`--state all`, no `status:backlog` filter — a drained-then-progressed story must not read as drift) via an exact-line `**Roadmap Source:**` marker match, and surfaces any genuinely untracked story as drift. This is the sprint-planning safety net for AC4 — the primary drain now happens at roadmap authoring time (`Product_Owner_Rules_template.md §11a`), not here.

descriptions..claude/agents/templates/rules/Technical: Fix (sprint-5 refine, ST-000026/027/028 design review): AC Clarifications (§2) gains a rule distinguishing it from the §7 'TL commenting on scope' red flag — narrowing an AC's technical interpretation stays TL's job, but a design answer that creates a genuinely new deliverable must flag PO rather than being folded in silently. The two rules previously gave conflicting guidance with no stated resolution.
descriptions..claude/agents/templates/rules/Story_Sta: Fix (sprint-5 refine): Role Boundaries §7 Red Flags line now points to `Technical_Lead_Rules.md §2` for how a routine AC-clarification edit differs from the 'TL commenting on scope' red flag, matching the companion fix in Technical_Lead_Rules_template.md.

Retro (#76, #78): Reviewer Gate (§12) gains an explicit branch for zero-checks-reported PRs — distinguishes 'nothing runnable changed' (path-filtered/`[skip ci]` docs-only commit, not a blocker) from 'CI genuinely missing' (do not approve without a real run or an explicit deviation note). descriptions..claude/agents/templates/rules/Developer: Retro (#76, #78): pre-PR checks table (§5) gains an explicit Lint/format row covering test files the implementer authored themselves, not only production source (#78 — a new regression test passed functionally but failed CI purely on an un-run lint check); Step 3 (§2) gains a mechanical `git branch --show-current` verification before the first commit, so implementation can no longer start directly on main/master/trunk undetected (#76).

descriptions..claude/agents/templates/rules/Developer: Fix (#48, #45, #47, #50): §5 cross-references Agent_Common.md §7 for missing-credential blocks; §11 Peer Review adds CI-execution-vs-conclusion, head-SHA-match, red-check-diagnosis, and stub/TODO re-check bullets alongside the reviewer rules TL now carries.
descriptions..claude/agents/templates/rules/Technical: Fix (#47, #50, #53, #48): §2 review checklist now confirms a CI check actually executed (not just its conclusion), confirms the cited run's head SHA matches the PR's current head, requires diagnosing red checks from their actual log, adds a dependency-pin resolvability check, and cross-references the missing-credential rule. New abbreviated 'CI/Workflow story' checklist (Technical Scope is `.github/workflows/**` only) mirroring the existing Documentation/Refactor checklists.
descriptions..claude/agents/templates/rules/QA_Rules_: Fix (#48, #45, #47, #53, #44): §4 adds a missing-credential example to the integration-test-skip escalation list, a real-fixture-test requirement wherever AC implies external integration, a 'mock/structural pass ≠ complete' rule, the run-twice (full-batch + isolated) technique for elevated verification bars, and CI/workflow-only + verification-only exceptions to the test-scenario-document requirement. §8 adds a CI-equivalent exception so a CI/workflow-only story's automation regression run isn't re-run 3x.
descriptions..claude/agents/templates/rules/Story_Sta: Fix (#52): §12 Reviewer checklist now requires pasting the literal `gh pr checks <PR#>` output into the approval comment as an auditable artifact, closing the gap where a TL approved a PR while CI was still running with no way to catch it after the fact.
descriptions..claude/agents/templates/rules/CICD_Vali: Fix (#50): new named exception — a new CI check's first red run on genuine application assertions (not its own setup/infra) is an expected, acceptable gate outcome, not something to work around.
descriptions..claude/agents/templates/rules/Clean_Cod: Fix (#53): 'Skip for' list now explicitly names `.github/workflows/`/CI YAML files, removing ambiguity that previously left this inferred from 'config-only'.
descriptions..claude/agents/templates/shared/workflow: Fix (#52, #45, #47, #50, #44): Merge Procedure gets a mandatory step 0 CI-check gate (`gh pr checks`) independent of reviewer sign-off — real incident had 3 stories merge while CI was red on 6 consecutive runs. Fix (#46): API surface check now requires, for multi-repo sibling-contract endpoints, a closed review-scoped story actually covering the endpoint's schema — not just path existence in the spec file.

Fix (#46): new cross-repo dependency audit before locking a sprint — verifies the owning repo has a closed review story whose AC scope covers every contract endpoint the sprint's stories touch, surfacing gaps as planning blockers.

Fix (#45): Batch Retro Review's `[context]` routing now asks explicitly whether a note describes a missing capability with no owning backlog story, routing it to backlog creation instead of only a priming/memory edit.
